summary.text: Michael McGuire is a family law attorney, U.S. Marine Corps veteran, U.S. Navy Reserve member and former New York City police officer. He won the Republican nomination for NJ-3 in the June 2, 2026 primary and has not previously held elected office. He says he is running on affordability, veterans' issues and term limits for members of Congress.

paragraphs.text: McGuire served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1997 to 2001 and subsequently in the U.S. Navy Reserve, where he remains a member.

WHYY reports that after four years in the Marines he joined the New York City Police Department, where he was a first responder on September 11, 2001; he describes his background as including service as a law enforcement officer.
He works as an attorney, and the New Jersey Globe describes his practice as family law and divorce; WHYY adds that he is a small-business advisor and tax practitioner.
McGuire lives in Freehold Township, according to the New Jersey Globe.
McGuire told the New Jersey Globe that he had run for school board in the past; WHYY describes the congressional campaign as his first run for office.
The Globe reported that his decision to run for Congress followed the fall 2025 federal government shutdown, during which he and fellow Navy reservists missed paychecks.
He launched his campaign in January 2026 and defeated Jason Cullen and Justin Barbera in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 57.9% of the vote.

Ballotpedia lists endorsements from Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden, former U.S. Rep. Barry Morris Goldwater Jr., the Monmouth County Republican Committee and the Mercer County Republican Committee.
